newsitem.title: INDIA: Weak world trends impact on India gold prices.
newsitem.headline: Weak world trends impact on India gold prices.

text.p: ** Indian 24 carat gold prices on Thursday open 10 rupees
lower at 4,630 rupees per 10 grammes on weak world trends
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) up 100 rupees
** Silver (.999) starts 40 rupees lower at 6,700 rupees per
kg against the previous close of 6,740 rupees
Indian 24 carat gold prices on Thursday opened 10 rupees lower at 4,630 rupees per 10 grammes on weak world market trends, triggering fresh selling, dealers said.
Imported gold arrivals slowed and the end of seasonal demand also subdued market sentiment in early trade.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) opened 100 rupees lower at 54,200 rupees against the previous close of 54,300 rupees.
Silver (.999) opened 40 rupees lower at 6,700 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,740 rupees as stockists booked profits on reports of a setback in the world market.
Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
Overall volume for both the precious metals remained at a low ebb in opening trade.
